statement: In declarative sentences with nominal subject and object, the dominant order is almost always one in which the object precedes the subject.
antecedent: declarative sentence with nominal subject and object
consequent: object precedes subject in dominant order

statement: When a yes-no question is marked by a single morpheme, it is not differentiated from the corresponding declarative by intonation or by a characteristic position of the morpheme at the beginning or end of the sentence.
antecedent: yes-no question is marked by a single morpheme
consequent: the question morpheme is not differentiated from declarative by intonation or by sentence-peripheral position

statement: In conditional statements, the conclusion precedes the conditional clause as the normal order in all languages.
consequent: conclusion precedes the conditional clause as normal order

statement: When the descriptive adjective precedes the noun, the demonstrative and the numeral, with overwhelmingly more than chance frequency, follow the noun.
consequent: demonstrative and numeral follow the noun

statement: If the pronominal object follows the verb, the nominal object precedes the verb.
If a language has inflection, it does not have derivation.
consequent: language does not have derivational morphology

statement: If the verb has categories of person-number or of gender, it does not have tense-mode categories.
antecedent: verb has categories of person-number or of gender
consequent: verb does not have tense-mode (tense or mood) categories

statement: A language may have a dual even if it has no other nonsingular number category.
antecedent: language has a dual number category
consequent: language has no other nonsingular number category

statement: If a language has the category of gender, it does not have the category of number.
consequent: language does not have grammatical number

statement: All languages have pronominal categories involving fewer than three persons or fewer than two numbers.
consequent: language has fewer than three person distinctions or fewer than two number distinctions in pronouns
